title: Idioms for everyday situations and feelings
title_uz: Kundalik vaziyatlar va his-tuyg‘ular haqidagi iboralar

words.ex: Our plan to surprise the coach worked like a dream: she had no idea until she opened the door.
The school open day went like clockwork: every guide was in place and every talk started on time.
After the technician fixed the server, the school website was back up and running within an hour.
The bus is booked and the permission slips are signed: the pieces of the class trip are finally falling into place.
After a terrible start to the season, things are looking up for our volleyball team: we've won our last three matches.
We're already late, and now the bus has broken down? Oh no, that's all we need!

words.en: the last thing I wanted to hear
words.ex: The mechanic said the repair would take another month, which was the last thing I wanted to hear.
words.gap: the last thing I wanted to hear
alt: last thing I wanted to hear

words.ex: First the car wouldn't start, then I missed the train, then it began to snow; the whole day was like a bad dream.
I'd do anything to avoid it: speaking in front of five hundred people is my worst nightmare.
The lift is broken again, so we'll have to carry the boxes up nine floors: what a pain!
When the interviewer suddenly switched to Russian halfway through, it threw me, and I needed a moment to recover.
With no microphone, no chairs and no printed programme, the prize-giving ceremony was a complete shambles.
How my little brother finishes his homework in ten minutes is a mystery to me.
Otabek and I got our wires crossed: he waited at the north exit of the metro while I stood at the south one for half an hour.
Sorry, I'm not with you; which form do I need to sign first?
Wait, you've lost me there: what does 'depreciation' actually mean?
Shohruh has been on cloud nine since he heard he'd won a place at the music academy.
Put Zuhra in a kitchen full of hungry guests and she's in her element.
With her calm voice and endless patience, Zarnigor was made for teaching small children.

words.en: fed up to the back teeth
words.ex: The residents are fed up to the back teeth with the noise from the building site next door.
words.gap: fed up to the back teeth

words.ex: Bahrom has been down in the dumps since his football team lost the cup final.
Why are you looking so down in the mouth? Cheer up, it's the weekend!
Driving through the city centre on the Friday before a holiday is a real nightmare: it took us an hour to go three kilometres.
